2609.30094.title: PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations
2609.30094.paper_summary: Large language models increasingly operate as persistent assistants in user-facing, shared-session, and tool-augmented settings. When users disclose sensitive information during an active conversation, that information may remain behaviorally recoverable through later prompts even after the dialogue shifts to unrelated topics. We introduce \textbf{PrivDrift}, a benchmark for auditing whether user-disclosed secrets remain recoverable after conversational topic drift and persuasion-based probing. PrivDrift contains 1{,}000 controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, content-dense drift turns, and standardized extraction probes. Across three LLMs with extended context windows, dialogue-level hybrid leakage remains substantial, ranging from 38.7\% to 54.6\%, and varies strongly by model, secret type, and persuasion intensity. Within the tested drift window, additional topic drift does not reliably reduce leakage, suggesting that privacy risk in active LLM contexts should be evaluated as a persistent behavioral failure mode rather than only as training-data memorization or immediate jailbreak behavior.
2609.30094.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型越來越多地作為持續的助手運作於面向用戶的共享會話和工具增強的環境中。當用戶在主動對話中透露敏感信息時，即使對話轉向無關主題，該信息仍可能在後續提示中被行為性地恢復。我們介紹了 \textbf{PrivDrift}，這是一個基準，用於審核用戶披露的秘密在對話主題漂移和基於說服的探測後是否仍然可以恢復。PrivDrift 包含 1{,}000 個受控的多輪對話，帶有種子秘密、內容密集的漂移輪次和標準化的提取探針。在三個具有擴展上下文窗口的 LLM 中，對話級別的混合洩漏仍然相當可觀，範圍從 38.7\% 到 54.6\%，並且根據模型、秘密類型和說服強度有很大的變化。在測試的漂移窗口內，額外的主題漂移並不可靠地減少洩漏，這表明在主動 LLM 環境中，隱私風險應被評估為一種持續的行為失效模式，而不僅僅是訓練數據的記憶或即時越獄行為。
2609.30094.author: Luciano Maldonado et.al.
